The actuator forces are defined as
$\uact=[F_{X1}\;F_{X2}\;F_Y]^\top$ and the measured positions
$\qact=[X_1\;X_2\;Y]^\top$.
Here $F_{X1}$, $F_{X2}$ and $F_Y$ are the forces and
$X_1$, $X_2$ and $Y$ the measured positions of the
\chg[Dirk]{two X actuators and the Y actuator}{two X and the Y actuators}%
\add[Q17]{\kwtwo{, each from a linear encoder~\cite{garcia2013model}}}.
% FEEDBACK v1 (2026-10-21): Q17 ("add location of encoders"): Garcia Sec.
%   2.1 (PDF p2), each actuator has a linear encoder that measures its
%   position. Js22 ("positions of what? the stages?"): no change, "of the
%   two X actuators and the Y actuator" is Garcia's wording (Sec. 2.2, PDF
%   p3: (X1, X2, Y) are the measured positions of the actuators)
%   (Dirk 2026-10-21).
\\
The system to be identified is the gantry system
described \chg{as,}{by}
\begin{equation}
  \dot x(t)=f\bigl(x(t),\uact(t)\bigr),\qquad y_k=\qact(kT_s)+v_k,
  \label{eq:system}
\end{equation}
% where the \kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
% positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
% sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
% The state-transition function $f$ is unknown.
where the \chg[own]{\kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
positions $\qact$}}{state $x$ contains the actuator positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
The \chg[own]{state-transition function $f$ is}{function $f$ and the
dimension of $x$ are} unknown.
The system runs in closed loop with an assumed known
linear time-invariant feedback controller\del[M-p3]{ (Section~\ref{sec:aug_loop})},
which gives the data set $\mathcal D_N=\{u_{\mathrm{act},k},y_k\}_{k=1}^N$.
% \add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the reference
% $r_k$ and the measured positions, and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is
% added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the
error between the reference $r_k$ and the measured positions $y_k$,
and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 x^{\mathrm{fb}}_{k+1}&=A_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+B_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k),\\
 u_{\mathrm{act},k}&=C_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+D_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k)+u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:system_loop}
\end{equation}
\mv[M-p3]{IV-B}{where $(A_{\mathrm{fb}},B_{\mathrm{fb}},C_{\mathrm{fb}},D_{\mathrm{fb}})$
are the state-space matrices of the controller\add[own]{ $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}\add[M-p3]{, with state
$x^{\mathrm{fb}}$,} discretised
with sampling time $T_s$\add[own]{\kwtwo{, and the actuator forces are held
constant between samples, $\uact(t)=u_{\mathrm{act},k}$ for
$kT_s\le t<(k+1)T_s$}}.
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-21): the hold links the continuous-time
%   eq:system to the discrete eq:system_loop; Section II states the

%   the second-opinion session sec2-rate-review against Clean/gantry_dynamic
%   and the Simulink model (Dirk 2026-10-21).
Both $r_k$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ are in actuator coordinates.}
% \add[M-p3]{The noise $v_k$ is independent of $r$ and
% $u^{\mathrm{ff}}$\add[M-p3]{\kwtwo{, but through the feedback it is
% correlated with $u_{\mathrm{act}}$}}.}
\add[M-p3]{The noise $v$ is independent of $r$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}$.
The force $u_{\mathrm{act}}$ is correlated with $v$, because the
controller computes it from $y$.}

We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} as our
physics-based baseline model of \eqref{eq:system}.
This model does not capture all dynamics of the system.
We identify these missing dynamics from $\mathcal D_N$ and augment the
baseline with learned components and additional
states~\cite{hoekstra2026lfr}.
% \mv[Jan7]{III intro}{A correction to the states of the baseline model alone is 
% not sufficient,
% \kwtwo{because missing dynamics need states the baseline does not 
% have\del[M-mail]{
% (Section~\ref{sec:aug_structure})},}
% so additional states are introduced.
\\
The goal is to estimate the \kw{physical and learned parameters} of the
augmented model from $\mathcal D_N$, such that it captures the missing
dynamics and accurately predicts the system, while the identifiable
combinations of the physical parameters are estimated uniquely.
% \mv[Jan23]{IV-C}{The model is trained using short windows of the
% closed-loop data, where each window is simulated with
% \chg[own]{the known controller}{the controller $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}.
% The initial states are estimated by \chg[Q37]{an encoder}{an encoder network}, 
% including the additional states.}
% \add[M-p7]{\kwtwo{This is the SUBNET method of Beintema et
% al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet}: the encoder estimates each initial state
% from past inputs and outputs and is trained jointly with the model.}}
We use the SUBNET method of Beintema et
al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet} to train the model on short windows of
$\mathcal D_N$, where each window is simulated with the controller
$K_{\mathrm{fb}}$.
The initial states are estimated by an encoder network from past inputs and outputs.

\subsection{Equations of motion}\label{sec:baseline}
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "state we leave out coulomb friction" is
%   covered by the friction sentence below.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): first sentence struck, it repeats Section II
%   (02_system_baseline.tex, "We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig. 1 as
%   our physics-based baseline model"). Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3): Eqs. (3) to
%   (5) are only T, V and D; substituting them with the forces (6) into the
%   Lagrange equation (7) gives the equations of motion (8) in X, Theta, Y.
\del[Dirk]{The physics baseline of the gantry system used in this thesis
is the lumped-parameter model of the
dual-drive gantry of Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\mbox{\cite{garcia2013model}}.}
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): source of the 3x3 matrices; Garcia prints only the
%   2x2 X-Theta matrices, Eqs. (12) to (17). The 3x3 form comes from the ASMPT
%   implementation (kamtin-fp-model/02 EulerLagrange/EulerLagrange.m).
Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.\ derive the equations of motion of the model
in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} from the Euler-Lagrange equations
\cite[Eqs.~(3) to~(8)]{garcia2013model}.
Let $L_b$ denote the cross-arm length between the two flexible joints.
The generalised coordinates $q=[X\;\Theta\;Y]^\top$ are defined as 
$X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ and 
$\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$, the position and yaw angle of
the cross-arm, while $Y$ is unchanged.
% NOTE (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Eq. (1) (PDF p3) defines
%   Theta = asin((X1-X2)/L_b); ours is its small-angle form (sin Theta ~ Theta),
%   to be made explicit in the small-angle assumption below, not here.
% \kw{These coordinates avoid
% a closed kinematic-chain description and make the coupling 
% associated with the
% \chg[Dirk]{nonuniform load distribution}{\kwtwo{load distribution over $X_1$ and $X_2$, which changes with the payload position $Y$,}} explicit \cite{garcia2013model}.}
These coordinates avoid closed kinematic chains when defining the
kinematics~\cite{garcia2013model}.
They also show the coupling caused by the non-uniform load distribution
between actuators $X_1$ and $X_2$, from the payload and differences in
motor characteristics.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): todo "How to connect, nonuniform ... moving
%   payload position" resolved: Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3) attributes the
%   nonuniform load distribution to the payload, and PDF p8 to its variable
%   position; in M(Y) it is the entry (L_b/2)(m_1-m_2)-m_h Y. Todo "why we
%   choose for this realisation" closed: the sentence gives Garcia's reasons
%   (PDF p3).
% FEEDBACK: the green words were Dirk's own, inside the \todo, so the review
%   PDF read "These coordinates avoid [3]." (Jan12, Js26, Q19). Garcia Sec. 2.2
%   gives both reasons.
The coordinate and force transformations are
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  q &= P^{-\top}\qact,
  \qquad
  u = P\uact,\\
  P &=
  \begin{bmatrix}
    1 & 1 & 0\\
    L_b/2 & -L_b/2 & 0\\
    0 & 0 & 1
  \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:Ptransform}
\end{equation}
where $u$ denotes the generalised force.
% Here $X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ is the translation of the cross-arm centre, $\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$ its yaw angle, and $Y$ is unchanged. These coordinates avoid a closed kinematic-chain description \cite{garcia2013model}.
% Then, after the matrices:
% The payload position enters $M(Y)$ in two entries. 
% The coupling term $\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY$ links $X$ and $\Theta$ unless $m_hY=\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)$, 
% and the yaw inertia grows with $m_hY^2$. Moving the payload therefore changes 
% both the load distribution over the two drives and the inertia about the yaw axis. 
% The baseline keeps this dependence in linear parameter-varying (LPV) form, 
% with the measured position $Y$ as scheduling variable \cite{toth2010modeling}.
Following Garc\'ia-Herreros et al. \cite{garcia2013model}, the baseline assumes $\cos(\Theta)\approx1$ and $\sin(\Theta)\approx0$, 
valid for small yaw angles, and assumes that the Coriolis and centripetal force terms are
negligible compared to the inertia, damping, and stiffness forces.

% In Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_lfr}(a), the physics baseline components are depicted in black;
% the simulated ground-truth system additionally includes the light-grey absorber.
The actuator forces are defined as
$\uact=[F_{X1}\;F_{X2}\;F_Y]^\top$ and the measured positions
$\qact=[X_1\;X_2\;Y]^\top$.
Here $F_{X1}$, $F_{X2}$ and $F_Y$ are the forces and
$X_1$, $X_2$ and $Y$ the measured positions of the
\chg[Dirk]{two X actuators and the Y actuator}{two X and the Y actuators}%
\add[Q17]{\kwtwo{, each from a linear encoder~\cite{garcia2013model}}}.
% FEEDBACK v1 (2026-10-21): Q17 ("add location of encoders"): Garcia Sec.
%   2.1 (PDF p2), each actuator has a linear encoder that measures its
%   position. Js22 ("positions of what? the stages?"): no change, "of the
%   two X actuators and the Y actuator" is Garcia's wording (Sec. 2.2, PDF
%   p3: (X1, X2, Y) are the measured positions of the actuators)
%   (Dirk 2026-10-21).
\\
The system to be identified is the gantry system
described \chg{as,}{by}
\begin{equation}
  \dot x(t)=f\bigl(x(t),\uact(t)\bigr),\qquad y_k=\qact(kT_s)+v_k,
  \label{eq:system}
\end{equation}
% where the \kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
% positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
% sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
% The state-transition function $f$ is unknown.
where the \chg[own]{\kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
positions $\qact$}}{state $x$ contains the actuator positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
The \chg[own]{state-transition function $f$ is}{function $f$ and the
dimension of $x$ are} unknown.
The system runs in closed loop with an assumed known
linear time-invariant feedback controller\del[M-p3]{ (Section~\ref{sec:aug_loop})},
which gives the data set $\mathcal D_N=\{u_{\mathrm{act},k},y_k\}_{k=1}^N$.
% \add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the reference
% $r_k$ and the measured positions, and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is
% added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the
error between the reference $r_k$ and the measured positions $y_k$,
and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 x^{\mathrm{fb}}_{k+1}&=A_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+B_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k),\\
 u_{\mathrm{act},k}&=C_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+D_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k)+u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:system_loop}
\end{equation}
\mv[M-p3]{IV-B}{where $(A_{\mathrm{fb}},B_{\mathrm{fb}},C_{\mathrm{fb}},D_{\mathrm{fb}})$
are the state-space matrices of the controller\add[own]{ $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}\add[M-p3]{, with state
$x^{\mathrm{fb}}$,} discretised
with sampling time $T_s$\add[own]{\kwtwo{, and the actuator forces are held
constant between samples, $\uact(t)=u_{\mathrm{act},k}$ for
$kT_s\le t<(k+1)T_s$}}.
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-21): the hold links the continuous-time
%   eq:system to the discrete eq:system_loop; Section II states the
%   assumptions at T_s that Section IV implements (RK4 with the input held,

%   the second-opinion session sec2-rate-review against Clean/gantry_dynamic
%   and the Simulink model (Dirk 2026-10-21).
Both $r_k$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ are in actuator coordinates.}
% \add[M-p3]{The noise $v_k$ is independent of $r$ and
% $u^{\mathrm{ff}}$\add[M-p3]{\kwtwo{, but through the feedback it is
% correlated with $u_{\mathrm{act}}$}}.}
\add[M-p3]{The noise $v$ is independent of $r$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}$.
The force $u_{\mathrm{act}}$ is correlated with $v$, because the
controller computes it from $y$.}

We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} as our
physics-based baseline model of \eqref{eq:system}.
This model does not capture all dynamics of the system.
We identify these missing dynamics from $\mathcal D_N$ and augment the
baseline with learned components and additional
states~\cite{hoekstra2026lfr}.
% \mv[Jan7]{III intro}{A correction to the states of the baseline model alone is 
% not sufficient,
% \kwtwo{because missing dynamics need states the baseline does not 
% have\del[M-mail]{
% (Section~\ref{sec:aug_structure})},}
% so additional states are introduced.
\\
The goal is to estimate the \kw{physical and learned parameters} of the
augmented model from $\mathcal D_N$, such that it captures the missing
dynamics and accurately predicts the system, while the identifiable
combinations of the physical parameters are estimated uniquely.
% \mv[Jan23]{IV-C}{The model is trained using short windows of the
% closed-loop data, where each window is simulated with
% \chg[own]{the known controller}{the controller $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}.
% The initial states are estimated by \chg[Q37]{an encoder}{an encoder network}, 
% including the additional states.}
% \add[M-p7]{\kwtwo{This is the SUBNET method of Beintema et
% al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet}: the encoder estimates each initial state
% from past inputs and outputs and is trained jointly with the model.}}
We use the SUBNET method of Beintema et
al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet} to train the model on short windows of
$\mathcal D_N$, where each window is simulated with the controller
$K_{\mathrm{fb}}$.
The initial states are estimated by an encoder network from past inputs and outputs.

\subsection{Equations of motion}\label{sec:baseline}
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "state we leave out coulomb friction" is
%   covered by the friction sentence below.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): first sentence struck, it repeats Section II
%   (02_system_baseline.tex, "We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig. 1 as

\del[Dirk]{The physics baseline of the gantry system used in this thesis
is the lumped-parameter model of the
dual-drive gantry of Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\mbox{\cite{garcia2013model}}.}
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): source of the 3x3 matrices; Garcia prints only the
%   2x2 X-Theta matrices, Eqs. (12) to (17). The 3x3 form comes from the ASMPT
%   implementation (kamtin-fp-model/02 EulerLagrange/EulerLagrange.m).
Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.\ derive the equations of motion of the model
in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} from the Euler-Lagrange equations
\cite[Eqs.~(3) to~(8)]{garcia2013model}.
Let $L_b$ denote the cross-arm length between the two flexible joints.
The generalised coordinates $q=[X\;\Theta\;Y]^\top$ are defined as 
$X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ and 
$\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$, the position and yaw angle of
the cross-arm, while $Y$ is unchanged.
% NOTE (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Eq. (1) (PDF p3) defines
%   Theta = asin((X1-X2)/L_b); ours is its small-angle form (sin Theta ~ Theta),
%   to be made explicit in the small-angle assumption below, not here.
% \kw{These coordinates avoid
% a closed kinematic-chain description and make the coupling 
% associated with the
% \chg[Dirk]{nonuniform load distribution}{\kwtwo{load distribution over $X_1$ and $X_2$, which changes with the payload position $Y$,}} explicit \cite{garcia2013model}.}
These coordinates avoid closed kinematic chains when defining the
kinematics~\cite{garcia2013model}.
They also show the coupling caused by the non-uniform load distribution
between actuators $X_1$ and $X_2$, from the payload and differences in
motor characteristics.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): todo "How to connect, nonuniform ... moving
%   payload position" resolved: Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3) attributes the
%   nonuniform load distribution to the payload, and PDF p8 to its variable
%   position; in M(Y) it is the entry (L_b/2)(m_1-m_2)-m_h Y. Todo "why we
%   choose for this realisation" closed: the sentence gives Garcia's reasons
%   (PDF p3).
% FEEDBACK: the green words were Dirk's own, inside the \todo, so the review
%   PDF read "These coordinates avoid [3]." (Jan12, Js26, Q19). Garcia Sec. 2.2
%   gives both reasons.
The coordinate and force transformations are
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  q &= P^{-\top}\qact,
  \qquad
  u = P\uact,\\
  P &=
  \begin{bmatrix}
    1 & 1 & 0\\
    L_b/2 & -L_b/2 & 0\\
    0 & 0 & 1
  \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:Ptransform}
\end{equation}
where $u$ denotes the generalised force.
% Here $X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ is the translation of the cross-arm centre, $\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$ its yaw angle, and $Y$ is unchanged. These coordinates avoid a closed kinematic-chain description \cite{garcia2013model}.
% Then, after the matrices:
% The payload position enters $M(Y)$ in two entries. 
% The coupling term $\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY$ links $X$ and $\Theta$ unless $m_hY=\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)$, 
% and the yaw inertia grows with $m_hY^2$. Moving the payload therefore changes 
% both the load distribution over the two drives and the inertia about the yaw axis. 
% The baseline keeps this dependence in linear parameter-varying (LPV) form, 
% with the measured position $Y$ as scheduling variable \cite{toth2010modeling}.
Following Garc\'ia-Herreros et al. \cite{garcia2013model}, the baseline assumes $\cos(\Theta)\approx1$ and $\sin(\Theta)\approx0$, 
valid for small yaw angles, and assumes that the Coriolis and centripetal force terms are
negligible compared to the inertia, damping, and stiffness forces.
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Sec. 2.3 moves m_h d Ydd to the force
%   vector (Eq. 15) and treats Y separately (Eq. 17); the baseline keeps it in M.
%\kwtwo{Unlike~\cite[Sec.~2.3.1]{garcia2013model}, $M(Y)$ keeps the coupling $-m_hd$ between $\Theta$ and $Y$.}
Our baseline model does not include the Coulomb friction
of~\cite[Eq.~(6)]{garcia2013model}.
Instead, it is part of the missing dynamics of Section~\ref{sec:problem}.

We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} as our
physics-based baseline model of \eqref{eq:system}.
This model does not capture all dynamics of the system.
We identify these missing dynamics from $\mathcal D_N$ and augment the
baseline with learned components and additional
states~\cite{hoekstra2026lfr}.
% \mv[Jan7]{III intro}{A correction to the states of the baseline model alone is 
% not sufficient,
% \kwtwo{because missing dynamics need states the baseline does not 
% have\del[M-mail]{
% (Section~\ref{sec:aug_structure})},}
% so additional states are introduced.
\\
The goal is to estimate the \kw{physical and learned parameters} of the
augmented model from $\mathcal D_N$, such that it captures the missing
dynamics and accurately predicts the system, while the identifiable
combinations of the physical parameters are estimated uniquely.
% \mv[Jan23]{IV-C}{The model is trained using short windows of the
% closed-loop data, where each window is simulated with
% \chg[own]{the known controller}{the controller $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}.
% The initial states are estimated by \chg[Q37]{an encoder}{an encoder network}, 
% including the additional states.}
% \add[M-p7]{\kwtwo{This is the SUBNET method of Beintema et
% al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet}: the encoder estimates each initial state
% from past inputs and outputs and is trained jointly with the model.}}
We use the SUBNET method of Beintema et
al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet} to train the model on short windows of
$\mathcal D_N$, where each window is simulated with the controller
$K_{\mathrm{fb}}$.
The initial states are estimated by an encoder network from past inputs and outputs.

\subsection{Equations of motion}\label{sec:baseline}
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "state we leave out coulomb friction" is
%   covered by the friction sentence below.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): first sentence struck, it repeats Section II
%   (02_system_baseline.tex, "We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig. 1 as

\del[Dirk]{The physics baseline of the gantry system used in this thesis
is the lumped-parameter model of the
dual-drive gantry of Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\mbox{\cite{garcia2013model}}.}
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): source of the 3x3 matrices; Garcia prints only the
%   2x2 X-Theta matrices, Eqs. (12) to (17). The 3x3 form comes from the ASMPT
%   implementation (kamtin-fp-model/02 EulerLagrange/EulerLagrange.m).
Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.\ derive the equations of motion of the model
in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} from the Euler-Lagrange equations
\cite[Eqs.~(3) to~(8)]{garcia2013model}.
Let $L_b$ denote the cross-arm length between the two flexible joints.
The generalised coordinates $q=[X\;\Theta\;Y]^\top$ are defined as 
$X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ and 
$\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$, the position and yaw angle of
the cross-arm, while $Y$ is unchanged.
% NOTE (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Eq. (1) (PDF p3) defines
%   Theta = asin((X1-X2)/L_b); ours is its small-angle form (sin Theta ~ Theta),
%   to be made explicit in the small-angle assumption below, not here.
% \kw{These coordinates avoid
% a closed kinematic-chain description and make the coupling 
% associated with the
% \chg[Dirk]{nonuniform load distribution}{\kwtwo{load distribution over $X_1$ and $X_2$, which changes with the payload position $Y$,}} explicit \cite{garcia2013model}.}
These coordinates avoid closed kinematic chains when defining the
kinematics~\cite{garcia2013model}.
They also show the coupling caused by the non-uniform load distribution
between actuators $X_1$ and $X_2$, from the payload and differences in
motor characteristics.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): todo "How to connect, nonuniform ... moving
%   payload position" resolved: Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3) attributes the
%   nonuniform load distribution to the payload, and PDF p8 to its variable
%   position; in M(Y) it is the entry (L_b/2)(m_1-m_2)-m_h Y. Todo "why we
%   choose for this realisation" closed: the sentence gives Garcia's reasons
%   (PDF p3).
% FEEDBACK: the green words were Dirk's own, inside the \todo, so the review
%   PDF read "These coordinates avoid [3]." (Jan12, Js26, Q19). Garcia Sec. 2.2
%   gives both reasons.
The coordinate and force transformations are
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  q &= P^{-\top}\qact,
  \qquad
  u = P\uact,\\
  P &=
  \begin{bmatrix}
    1 & 1 & 0\\
    L_b/2 & -L_b/2 & 0\\
    0 & 0 & 1
  \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:Ptransform}
\end{equation}
where $u$ denotes the generalised force.
% Here $X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ is the translation of the cross-arm centre, $\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$ its yaw angle, and $Y$ is unchanged. These coordinates avoid a closed kinematic-chain description \cite{garcia2013model}.
% Then, after the matrices:
% The payload position enters $M(Y)$ in two entries. 
% The coupling term $\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY$ links $X$ and $\Theta$ unless $m_hY=\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)$, 
% and the yaw inertia grows with $m_hY^2$. Moving the payload therefore changes 
% both the load distribution over the two drives and the inertia about the yaw axis. 
% The baseline keeps this dependence in linear parameter-varying (LPV) form, 
% with the measured position $Y$ as scheduling variable \cite{toth2010modeling}.
Following Garc\'ia-Herreros et al. \cite{garcia2013model}, the baseline assumes $\cos(\Theta)\approx1$ and $\sin(\Theta)\approx0$, 
valid for small yaw angles, and assumes that the Coriolis and centripetal force terms are
negligible compared to the inertia, damping, and stiffness forces.
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Sec. 2.3 moves m_h d Ydd to the force
%   vector (Eq. 15) and treats Y separately (Eq. 17); the baseline keeps it in M.
%\kwtwo{Unlike~\cite[Sec.~2.3.1]{garcia2013model}, $M(Y)$ keeps the coupling $-m_hd$ between $\Theta$ and $Y$.}
Our baseline model does not include the Coulomb friction
of~\cite[Eq.~(6)]{garcia2013model}.
Instead, it is part of the missing dynamics of Section~\ref{sec:problem}.

The actuator forces are defined as
$\uact=[F_{X1}\;F_{X2}\;F_Y]^\top$ and the measured positions
$\qact=[X_1\;X_2\;Y]^\top$.
Here $F_{X1}$, $F_{X2}$ and $F_Y$ are the forces and
$X_1$, $X_2$ and $Y$ the measured positions of the
\chg[Dirk]{two X actuators and the Y actuator}{two X and the Y actuators}%
\add[Q17]{\kwtwo{, each from a linear encoder~\cite{garcia2013model}}}.
% FEEDBACK v1 (2026-10-21): Q17 ("add location of encoders"): Garcia Sec.
%   2.1 (PDF p2), each actuator has a linear encoder that measures its
%   position. Js22 ("positions of what? the stages?"): no change, "of the
%   two X actuators and the Y actuator" is Garcia's wording (Sec. 2.2, PDF
%   p3: (X1, X2, Y) are the measured positions of the actuators)
%   (Dirk 2026-10-21).
\\
The system to be identified is the gantry system
described \chg{as,}{by}
\begin{equation}
  \dot x(t)=f\bigl(x(t),\uact(t)\bigr),\qquad y_k=\qact(kT_s)+v_k,
  \label{eq:system}
\end{equation}
% where the \kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
% positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
% sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
% The state-transition function $f$ is unknown.
where the \chg[own]{\kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
positions $\qact$}}{state $x$ contains the actuator positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
The \chg[own]{state-transition function $f$ is}{function $f$ and the
dimension of $x$ are} unknown.
The system runs in closed loop with an assumed known
linear time-invariant feedback controller\del[M-p3]{ (Section~\ref{sec:aug_loop})},
which gives the data set $\mathcal D_N=\{u_{\mathrm{act},k},y_k\}_{k=1}^N$.
% \add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the reference
% $r_k$ and the measured positions, and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is
% added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the
error between the reference $r_k$ and the measured positions $y_k$,
and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 x^{\mathrm{fb}}_{k+1}&=A_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+B_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k),\\
 u_{\mathrm{act},k}&=C_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+D_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k)+u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:system_loop}
\end{equation}
\mv[M-p3]{IV-B}{where $(A_{\mathrm{fb}},B_{\mathrm{fb}},C_{\mathrm{fb}},D_{\mathrm{fb}})$
are the state-space matrices of the controller\add[own]{ $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}\add[M-p3]{, with state
$x^{\mathrm{fb}}$,} discretised
with sampling time $T_s$\add[own]{\kwtwo{, and the actuator forces are held
constant between samples, $\uact(t)=u_{\mathrm{act},k}$ for
$kT_s\le t<(k+1)T_s$}}.

%   the second-opinion session sec2-rate-review against Clean/gantry_dynamic
%   and the Simulink model (Dirk 2026-10-21).
Both $r_k$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ are in actuator coordinates.}

\add[M-p3]{The noise $v$ is independent of $r$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}$.
The force $u_{\mathrm{act}}$ is correlated with $v$, because the
controller computes it from $y$.}

\\
We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} as our
physics-based baseline model of \eqref{eq:system}.
This model does not capture all dynamics of the system.
We identify these missing dynamics from $\mathcal D_N$ and augment the
baseline with learned components and additional
states~\cite{hoekstra2026lfr}.
% \mv[Jan7]{III intro}{A correction to the states of the baseline model alone is 
% not sufficient,
% \kwtwo{because missing dynamics need states the baseline does not 
% have\del[M-mail]{
% (Section~\ref{sec:aug_structure})},}
% so additional states are introduced.
\\
The goal is to estimate the \kw{physical and learned parameters} of the
augmented model from $\mathcal D_N$, such that it captures the missing
dynamics and accurately predicts the system, while the identifiable
combinations of the physical parameters are estimated uniquely.
% \mv[Jan23]{IV-C}{The model is trained using short windows of the
% closed-loop data, where each window is simulated with
% \chg[own]{the known controller}{the controller $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}.
% The initial states are estimated by \chg[Q37]{an encoder}{an encoder network}, 
% including the additional states.}
% \add[M-p7]{\kwtwo{This is the SUBNET method of Beintema et
% al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet}: the encoder estimates each initial state
% from past inputs and outputs and is trained jointly with the model.}}
We use the SUBNET method of Beintema et
al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet} to train the model on short windows of
$\mathcal D_N$, where each window is simulated with the controller
$K_{\mathrm{fb}}$.
The initial states are estimated by an encoder network from past inputs and outputs.

\subsection{Equations of motion}\label{sec:baseline}
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "state we leave out coulomb friction" is
%   covered by the friction sentence below.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): first sentence struck, it repeats Section II
%   (02_system_baseline.tex, "We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig. 1 as
%   our physics-based baseline model"). Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3): Eqs. (3) to
%   (5) are only T, V and D; substituting them with the forces (6) into the
%   Lagrange equation (7) gives the equations of motion (8) in X, Theta, Y.
\del[Dirk]{The physics baseline of the gantry system used in this thesis
is the lumped-parameter model of the
dual-drive gantry of Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\mbox{\cite{garcia2013model}}.}
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): source of the 3x3 matrices; Garcia prints only the
%   2x2 X-Theta matrices, Eqs. (12) to (17). The 3x3 form comes from the ASMPT
%   implementation (kamtin-fp-model/02 EulerLagrange/EulerLagrange.m).
Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.\ derive the equations of motion of the model
in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} from the Euler-Lagrange equations
\cite[Eqs.~(3) to~(8)]{garcia2013model}.
Let $L_b$ denote the cross-arm length between the two flexible joints.
The generalised coordinates $q=[X\;\Theta\;Y]^\top$ are defined as 
$X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ and 
$\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$, the position and yaw angle of
the cross-arm, while $Y$ is unchanged.
% NOTE (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Eq. (1) (PDF p3) defines
%   Theta = asin((X1-X2)/L_b); ours is its small-angle form (sin Theta ~ Theta),
%   to be made explicit in the small-angle assumption below, not here.
% \kw{These coordinates avoid
% a closed kinematic-chain description and make the coupling 
% associated with the
% \chg[Dirk]{nonuniform load distribution}{\kwtwo{load distribution over $X_1$ and $X_2$, which changes with the payload position $Y$,}} explicit \cite{garcia2013model}.}
These coordinates avoid closed kinematic chains when defining the
kinematics~\cite{garcia2013model}.
They also show the coupling caused by the non-uniform load distribution
between actuators $X_1$ and $X_2$, from the payload and differences in
motor characteristics.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): todo "How to connect, nonuniform ... moving
%   payload position" resolved: Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3) attributes the
%   nonuniform load distribution to the payload, and PDF p8 to its variable
%   position; in M(Y) it is the entry (L_b/2)(m_1-m_2)-m_h Y. Todo "why we
%   choose for this realisation" closed: the sentence gives Garcia's reasons
%   (PDF p3).
% FEEDBACK: the green words were Dirk's own, inside the \todo, so the review
%   PDF read "These coordinates avoid [3]." (Jan12, Js26, Q19). Garcia Sec. 2.2
%   gives both reasons.
The coordinate and force transformations are
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  q &= P^{-\top}\qact,
  \qquad
  u = P\uact,\\
  P &=
  \begin{bmatrix}
    1 & 1 & 0\\
    L_b/2 & -L_b/2 & 0\\
    0 & 0 & 1
  \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:Ptransform}
\end{equation}
where $u$ denotes the generalised force.
% Here $X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ is the translation of the cross-arm centre, $\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$ its yaw angle, and $Y$ is unchanged. These coordinates avoid a closed kinematic-chain description \cite{garcia2013model}.
% Then, after the matrices:
% The payload position enters $M(Y)$ in two entries. 
% The coupling term $\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY$ links $X$ and $\Theta$ unless $m_hY=\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)$, 
% and the yaw inertia grows with $m_hY^2$. Moving the payload therefore changes 
% both the load distribution over the two drives and the inertia about the yaw axis. 
% The baseline keeps this dependence in linear parameter-varying (LPV) form, 
% with the measured position $Y$ as scheduling variable \cite{toth2010modeling}.
Following Garc\'ia-Herreros et al. \cite{garcia2013model}, the baseline assumes $\cos(\Theta)\approx1$ and $\sin(\Theta)\approx0$, 
valid for small yaw angles, and assumes that the Coriolis and centripetal force terms are
negligible compared to the inertia, damping, and stiffness forces.
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Sec. 2.3 moves m_h d Ydd to the force
%   vector (Eq. 15) and treats Y separately (Eq. 17); the baseline keeps it in M.
%\kwtwo{Unlike~\cite[Sec.~2.3.1]{garcia2013model}, $M(Y)$ keeps the coupling $-m_hd$ between $\Theta$ and $Y$.}
Our baseline model does not include the Coulomb friction
of~\cite[Eq.~(6)]{garcia2013model}.
Instead, it is part of the missing dynamics of Section~\ref{sec:problem}.
% TODO closed (2026-10-21): Sec. 2.2 checked, Garcia PDF p3 lists the Coulomb
%   forces c_c1, c_c2, c_cy of X1, X2 and Y.
% FEEDBACK: Q23 small angles; Garcia Sec. 2.2 (yaw limited to tens of
%   microrad in operation).
% The simulated ground-truth model uses the same simplifications.
Under these assumptions, the baseline equations of motion are
\begin{equation}
  M\bigl(Y(t)\bigr)\ddot{q}(t) + C\dot{q}(t) + K q(t) = u(t),
  \label{eq:eom}
\end{equation}
with
{\footnotesize
\setlength{\arraycolsep}{3pt}
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): matrices numbered as one group (4a) to (4c);
%   the shared C/K number dropped to its own line in the v2 build (p4).
%   eq:damping_stiffness_matrices kept on the group, as 03 and 99 cite it.
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:matrices}\label{eq:damping_stiffness_matrices}
\begin{equation}
M(Y)=
\begin{bmatrix}
m_1+m_2+m_b+m_h & \tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY & 0\\
\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY &
\substack{J_b+J_h+\tfrac{L_b^2}{4}(m_1+m_2)\\{}+m_h(d^2+Y^2)} & -m_hd\\
0 & -m_hd & m_h
\end{bmatrix},
\label{eq:mass_matrix}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
C=
\begin{bmatrix}
c_{g1}+c_{g2} & \tfrac{L_b}{2}(c_{g1}-c_{g2}) & 0\\
\tfrac{L_b}{2}(c_{g1}-c_{g2}) &
c_{b1}+c_{b2}+\tfrac{L_b^2}{4}(c_{g1}+c_{g2}) & 0\\
0 & 0 & c_y
\end{bmatrix},
\label{eq:damping_matrix}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
K=
\begin{bmatrix}
0&0&0\\
0&k_{b1}+k_{b2}&0\\
0&0&0
\end{bmatrix}.
\label{eq:stiffness_matrix}
\end{equation}
\end{subequations}
}
From here on the notation for the time dependency is dropped.
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "Proposed insertion" on Coulomb friction is
%   covered by the friction sentence above (reason in D-204); "Look at this
%   section" was a reading note.
The masses, \del[Dirk]{flexible-joint }stiffness and damping coefficients,
and dimensions $L_b$ and $d$ are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system}.
The two $X$ actuators have masses $m_1$ and $m_2$,
the cross-arm $m_b$ and the payload $m_h$.
The yaw inertias of the cross-arm and payload are $J_b$ and $J_h$.
The actuator damping coefficients are $c_{g1}$, $c_{g2}$ and $c_y$,
while the flexible joints have stiffness $k_{b1}$, $k_{b2}$
and damping $c_{b1}$, $c_{b2}$.
The distance between the centres of mass of the payload
and cross-arm is $d$~\cite{garcia2013model}.
The nominal values are taken from
\cite[Table~I]{garcia2013model} and listed in
Appendix~\ref{app:params}.

The actuator forces are defined as
$\uact=[F_{X1}\;F_{X2}\;F_Y]^\top$ and the measured positions
$\qact=[X_1\;X_2\;Y]^\top$.
Here $F_{X1}$, $F_{X2}$ and $F_Y$ are the forces and
$X_1$, $X_2$ and $Y$ the measured positions of the
\chg[Dirk]{two X actuators and the Y actuator}{two X and the Y actuators}%
\add[Q17]{\kwtwo{, each from a linear encoder~\cite{garcia2013model}}}.
% FEEDBACK v1 (2026-10-21): Q17 ("add location of encoders"): Garcia Sec.

\\
The system to be identified is the gantry system
described \chg{as,}{by}
\begin{equation}
  \dot x(t)=f\bigl(x(t),\uact(t)\bigr),\qquad y_k=\qact(kT_s)+v_k,
  \label{eq:system}
\end{equation}
% where the \kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
% positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
% sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
% The state-transition function $f$ is unknown.
where the \chg[own]{\kw{state $x$ is unknown, except that it contains the actuator
positions $\qact$}}{state $x$ contains the actuator positions $\qact$}, $y_k$ are the measured positions at sample $k$ with
sampling time $T_s$, and $v_k$ is zero-mean, coloured measurement noise.
The \chg[own]{state-transition function $f$ is}{function $f$ and the
dimension of $x$ are} unknown.
The system runs in closed loop with an assumed known
linear time-invariant feedback controller\del[M-p3]{ (Section~\ref{sec:aug_loop})},
which gives the data set $\mathcal D_N=\{u_{\mathrm{act},k},y_k\}_{k=1}^N$.
% \add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the reference
% $r_k$ and the measured positions, and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is
% added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\add[M-p3]{The controller computes the actuator forces from the
error between the reference $r_k$ and the measured positions $y_k$,
and a feedforward $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ is added (Fig.~\ref{fig:system_loop}):}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 x^{\mathrm{fb}}_{k+1}&=A_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+B_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k),\\
 u_{\mathrm{act},k}&=C_{\mathrm{fb}}x^{\mathrm{fb}}_k+D_{\mathrm{fb}}(r_k-y_k)+u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:system_loop}
\end{equation}
\mv[M-p3]{IV-B}{where $(A_{\mathrm{fb}},B_{\mathrm{fb}},C_{\mathrm{fb}},D_{\mathrm{fb}})$
are the state-space matrices of the controller\add[own]{ $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}\add[M-p3]{, with state
$x^{\mathrm{fb}}$,} discretised
with sampling time $T_s$\add[own]{\kwtwo{, and the actuator forces are held
constant between samples, $\uact(t)=u_{\mathrm{act},k}$ for
$kT_s\le t<(k+1)T_s$}}.

%   and the Simulink model (Dirk 2026-10-21).
Both $r_k$ and $u^{\mathrm{ff}}_k$ are in actuator coordinates.}

The force $u_{\mathrm{act}}$ is correlated with $v$, because the
controller computes it from $y$.}

 %   the eq:system_loop where-clause (C_fb is one of the four matrices of
 %   eq:system_loop; K_fb matches K_1 of Section V and the ff/fb pair; Maarten
 %   p6 notation consistency). Gantry output stays q_act; the sampling and
 %   hold are stated in the text. No marks in figures and captions
 %   (Dirk 2026-10-21).
 \label{fig:system_loop}
\end{figure}
\\
We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} as our
physics-based baseline model of \eqref{eq:system}.
This model does not capture all dynamics of the system.
We identify these missing dynamics from $\mathcal D_N$ and augment the
baseline with learned components and additional
states~\cite{hoekstra2026lfr}.
% \mv[Jan7]{III intro}{A correction to the states of the baseline model alone is 
% not sufficient,
% \kwtwo{because missing dynamics need states the baseline does not 
% have\del[M-mail]{
% (Section~\ref{sec:aug_structure})},}
% so additional states are introduced.
\\
The goal is to estimate the \kw{physical and learned parameters} of the
augmented model from $\mathcal D_N$, such that it captures the missing
dynamics and accurately predicts the system, while the identifiable
combinations of the physical parameters are estimated uniquely.
% \mv[Jan23]{IV-C}{The model is trained using short windows of the
% closed-loop data, where each window is simulated with
% \chg[own]{the known controller}{the controller $K_{\mathrm{fb}}$}.
% The initial states are estimated by \chg[Q37]{an encoder}{an encoder network}, 
% including the additional states.}
% \add[M-p7]{\kwtwo{This is the SUBNET method of Beintema et
% al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet}: the encoder estimates each initial state
% from past inputs and outputs and is trained jointly with the model.}}
We use the SUBNET method of Beintema et
al.~\cite{beintema2023subnet} to train the model on short windows of
$\mathcal D_N$, where each window is simulated with the controller
$K_{\mathrm{fb}}$.
The initial states are estimated by an encoder network from past inputs and outputs.

\subsection{Equations of motion}\label{sec:baseline}
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "state we leave out coulomb friction" is
%   covered by the friction sentence below.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): first sentence struck, it repeats Section II
%   (02_system_baseline.tex, "We use the lumped-parameter model of Fig. 1 as
%   our physics-based baseline model"). Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3): Eqs. (3) to
%   (5) are only T, V and D; substituting them with the forces (6) into the
%   Lagrange equation (7) gives the equations of motion (8) in X, Theta, Y.
\del[Dirk]{The physics baseline of the gantry system used in this thesis
is the lumped-parameter model of the
dual-drive gantry of Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\mbox{\cite{garcia2013model}}.}
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): source of the 3x3 matrices; Garcia prints only the
%   2x2 X-Theta matrices, Eqs. (12) to (17). The 3x3 form comes from the ASMPT
%   implementation (kamtin-fp-model/02 EulerLagrange/EulerLagrange.m).
Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.\ derive the equations of motion of the model
in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system} from the Euler-Lagrange equations
\cite[Eqs.~(3) to~(8)]{garcia2013model}.
Let $L_b$ denote the cross-arm length between the two flexible joints.
The generalised coordinates $q=[X\;\Theta\;Y]^\top$ are defined as 
$X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ and 
$\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$, the position and yaw angle of
the cross-arm, while $Y$ is unchanged.
% NOTE (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Eq. (1) (PDF p3) defines
%   Theta = asin((X1-X2)/L_b); ours is its small-angle form (sin Theta ~ Theta),
%   to be made explicit in the small-angle assumption below, not here.
% \kw{These coordinates avoid
% a closed kinematic-chain description and make the coupling 
% associated with the
% \chg[Dirk]{nonuniform load distribution}{\kwtwo{load distribution over $X_1$ and $X_2$, which changes with the payload position $Y$,}} explicit \cite{garcia2013model}.}
These coordinates avoid closed kinematic chains when defining the
kinematics~\cite{garcia2013model}.
They also show the coupling caused by the non-uniform load distribution
between actuators $X_1$ and $X_2$, from the payload and differences in
motor characteristics.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): todo "How to connect, nonuniform ... moving
%   payload position" resolved: Garcia Sec. 2.2 (PDF p3) attributes the
%   nonuniform load distribution to the payload, and PDF p8 to its variable
%   position; in M(Y) it is the entry (L_b/2)(m_1-m_2)-m_h Y. Todo "why we
%   choose for this realisation" closed: the sentence gives Garcia's reasons
%   (PDF p3).
% FEEDBACK: the green words were Dirk's own, inside the \todo, so the review
%   PDF read "These coordinates avoid [3]." (Jan12, Js26, Q19). Garcia Sec. 2.2
%   gives both reasons.
The coordinate and force transformations are
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  q &= P^{-\top}\qact,
  \qquad
  u = P\uact,\\
  P &=
  \begin{bmatrix}
    1 & 1 & 0\\
    L_b/2 & -L_b/2 & 0\\
    0 & 0 & 1
  \end{bmatrix},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:Ptransform}
\end{equation}
where $u$ denotes the generalised force.
% Here $X=(X_1+X_2)/2$ is the translation of the cross-arm centre, $\Theta=(X_1-X_2)/L_b$ its yaw angle, and $Y$ is unchanged. These coordinates avoid a closed kinematic-chain description \cite{garcia2013model}.
% Then, after the matrices:
% The payload position enters $M(Y)$ in two entries. 
% The coupling term $\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY$ links $X$ and $\Theta$ unless $m_hY=\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)$, 
% and the yaw inertia grows with $m_hY^2$. Moving the payload therefore changes 
% both the load distribution over the two drives and the inertia about the yaw axis. 
% The baseline keeps this dependence in linear parameter-varying (LPV) form, 
% with the measured position $Y$ as scheduling variable \cite{toth2010modeling}.
Following Garc\'ia-Herreros et al. \cite{garcia2013model}, the baseline assumes $\cos(\Theta)\approx1$ and $\sin(\Theta)\approx0$, 
valid for small yaw angles, and assumes that the Coriolis and centripetal force terms are
negligible compared to the inertia, damping, and stiffness forces.
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): Garcia Sec. 2.3 moves m_h d Ydd to the force
%   vector (Eq. 15) and treats Y separately (Eq. 17); the baseline keeps it in M.
%\kwtwo{Unlike~\cite[Sec.~2.3.1]{garcia2013model}, $M(Y)$ keeps the coupling $-m_hd$ between $\Theta$ and $Y$.}
Our baseline model does not include the Coulomb friction
of~\cite[Eq.~(6)]{garcia2013model}.
Instead, it is part of the missing dynamics of Section~\ref{sec:problem}.
% TODO closed (2026-10-21): Sec. 2.2 checked, Garcia PDF p3 lists the Coulomb
%   forces c_c1, c_c2, c_cy of X1, X2 and Y.
% FEEDBACK: Q23 small angles; Garcia Sec. 2.2 (yaw limited to tens of
%   microrad in operation).
% The simulated ground-truth model uses the same simplifications.
Under these assumptions, the baseline equations of motion are
\begin{equation}
  M\bigl(Y(t)\bigr)\ddot{q}(t) + C\dot{q}(t) + K q(t) = u(t),
  \label{eq:eom}
\end{equation}
with
{\footnotesize
\setlength{\arraycolsep}{3pt}
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-21, Dirk): matrices numbered as one group (4a) to (4c);
%   the shared C/K number dropped to its own line in the v2 build (p4).
%   eq:damping_stiffness_matrices kept on the group, as 03 and 99 cite it.
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:matrices}\label{eq:damping_stiffness_matrices}
\begin{equation}
M(Y)=
\begin{bmatrix}
m_1+m_2+m_b+m_h & \tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY & 0\\
\tfrac{L_b}{2}(m_1-m_2)-m_hY &
\substack{J_b+J_h+\tfrac{L_b^2}{4}(m_1+m_2)\\{}+m_h(d^2+Y^2)} & -m_hd\\
0 & -m_hd & m_h
\end{bmatrix},
\label{eq:mass_matrix}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
C=
\begin{bmatrix}
c_{g1}+c_{g2} & \tfrac{L_b}{2}(c_{g1}-c_{g2}) & 0\\
\tfrac{L_b}{2}(c_{g1}-c_{g2}) &
c_{b1}+c_{b2}+\tfrac{L_b^2}{4}(c_{g1}+c_{g2}) & 0\\
0 & 0 & c_y
\end{bmatrix},
\label{eq:damping_matrix}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
K=
\begin{bmatrix}
0&0&0\\
0&k_{b1}+k_{b2}&0\\
0&0&0
\end{bmatrix}.
\label{eq:stiffness_matrix}
\end{equation}
\end{subequations}
}
From here on the notation for the time dependency is dropped.
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): "Proposed insertion" on Coulomb friction is
%   covered by the friction sentence above (reason in D-204); "Look at this
%   section" was a reading note.
The masses, \del[Dirk]{flexible-joint }stiffness and damping coefficients,
and dimensions $L_b$ and $d$ are shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system}.
The two $X$ actuators have masses $m_1$ and $m_2$,
the cross-arm $m_b$ and the payload $m_h$.
The yaw inertias of the cross-arm and payload are $J_b$ and $J_h$.
The actuator damping coefficients are $c_{g1}$, $c_{g2}$ and $c_y$,
while the flexible joints have stiffness $k_{b1}$, $k_{b2}$
and damping $c_{b1}$, $c_{b2}$.
The distance between the centres of mass of the payload
and cross-arm is $d$~\cite{garcia2013model}.
The nominal values are taken from
\cite[Table~I]{garcia2013model} and listed in
Appendix~\ref{app:params}.
% TODO closed (2026-10-21, Dirk): the sentence stays; the simulation uses the
%   Table I values (todo was "not identified on the present Telica machine").
% FEEDBACK: "geometric dimensions" were Di

\ifdraft
\begin{itemize}
\item The data is simulated: the system is the baseline plus rail friction and a payload absorber, both absent from the baseline
\item The friction subtracts from the actuator forces; a smoothed Coulomb law, Coulomb-like on the excited records
\item The absorber adds one coordinate, coupled through the inertia; matrices written out as in Section~II
\item Parameter values with their basis; both absorber features lie above the crossover of the loop
\item One known controller $K_1$, the same in every record; the injected force is the only feedforward
\item Noise matched to the machine; noise-free twin of every record; SNR (?: confidentiality)
\end{itemize}

% FEEDBACK (Dirk 2026-10-24): figure named in the text, in Dirk's pattern
%   ("Fig. 3 shows how ..."); friction sentence in Dirk's words.
The system used to generate the data consists of the baseline model \eqref{eq:eom}
with two additions.
\add[own]{\kwtwo{Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_absorber} shows the baseline model with
both additions.}}
The first is Coulomb friction at the actuators $X_1$, $X_2$ and $Y$, as
modelled by Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\cite{garcia2013model}.
We left it out of the baseline to add nonlinear unmodelled dynamics to the
system, for the augmented model to capture.
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-24): the display lead-in states this (Dirk 2026-10-24).
\del[own]{The friction works as a force against each actuator
force, this is modelled as a term entering \mbox{\eqref{eq:eom}} through the input.}
For the second addition, we split the payload mass $m_h$ into
$m_a$ and $m_{h,r}=m_h-m_a$, with $m_a$ connected to $m_{h,r}$
by a spring and damper in the $Y$ direction\del[own]{
(Fig.~\mbox{\ref{fig:gantry_absorber}})}.
This adds a vibration mode which the 
baseline model is not able to represent with its states.
\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{\input{figures/gantry_system_with_absorber}}
  % FEEDBACK (Jasper v1 p. 9, 2026-10-24): caption out of its \todo; friction
  %   drawn in grey at the force labels ("indicate the friction too"); no
  %   marks in captions (Dirk 2026-10-24).
  % FEEDBACK (Dirk 2026-10-24): caption rewritten in Dirk's words, with a
  %   reference to the baseline figure.
  \caption{Simulated system: the model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system}
  with an added mass, spring and damper on the payload, and friction
  $F_{\mathrm{fr}}$ at the actuators. Grey elements represent the
  unmodelled dynamics of the baseline.}
  \label{fig:gantry_absorber}
\end{figure}
With the friction acting against each actuator force on the input, 
\eqref{eq:eom} becomes
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:setup_truth}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 M(Y)\ddot q+C\dot q+Kq&=P\bigl(\uact-F_{\mathrm{fr}}(P^\top\dot q)\bigr),\\
 F_{\mathrm{fr},i}(v_i)&=c_{c,i}\tanh\bigl(v_i/v_{\mathrm{fr}}\bigr),
\end{aligned}
 \label{eq:setup_fric}
\end{equation}
% FEEDBACK (Jasper, 2026-10-24): v_i defined (undefined variables; walk
%   W2, Dirk 2026-10-24).
where $v_i$ is the velocity of actuator $i\in\{X_1,X_2,Y\}$,
with the actuator velocities given by $P^\top\dot q$,
and $v_{\mathrm{fr}}$ sets the velocity scale of the smoothing.
For $\lvert v_i\rvert\gg v_{\mathrm{fr}}$, the friction
approaches the Coulomb law
$F_{\mathrm{fr},i}=c_{c,i}\operatorname{sign}(v_i)$
of~\cite{garcia2013model}.

%   v_fr tuning moved to Appendix F-C, next to its 3 v_fr check (Dirk 2026-10-24).
\mv[own]{below}{The friction levels $c_c$ are taken from Garc\'ia-Herreros et
al.

both additions.}}
The first is Coulomb friction at the actuators $X_1$, $X_2$ and $Y$, as
modelled by Garc\'ia-Herreros et al.~\cite{garcia2013model}.
We left it out of the baseline to add nonlinear unmodelled dynamics to the
system, for the augmented model to capture.
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-24): the display lead-in states this (Dirk 2026-10-24).
\del[own]{The friction works as a force against each actuator
force, this is modelled as a term entering \mbox{\eqref{eq:eom}} through the input.}
For the second addition, we split the payload mass $m_h$ into
$m_a$ and $m_{h,r}=m_h-m_a$, with $m_a$ connected to $m_{h,r}$
by a spring and damper in the $Y$ direction\del[own]{
(Fig.~\mbox{\ref{fig:gantry_absorber}})}.
This adds a vibration mode which the 
baseline model is not able to represent with its states.
\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{\input{figures/gantry_system_with_absorber}}
  % FEEDBACK (Jasper v1 p. 9, 2026-10-24): caption out of its \todo; friction
  %   drawn in grey at the force labels ("indicate the friction too"); no
  %   marks in captions (Dirk 2026-10-24).
  % FEEDBACK (Dirk 2026-10-24): caption rewritten in Dirk's words, with a
  %   reference to the baseline figure.
  \caption{Simulated system: the model of Fig.~\ref{fig:gantry_system}
  with an added mass, spring and damper on the payload, and friction
  $F_{\mathrm{fr}}$ at the actuators. Grey elements represent the
  unmodelled dynamics of the baseline.}
  \label{fig:gantry_absorber}
\end{figure}
With the friction acting against each actuator force on the input, 
\eqref{eq:eom} becomes
\begin{subequations}\label{eq:setup_truth}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 M(Y)\ddot q+C\dot q+Kq&=P\bigl(\uact-F_{\mathrm{fr}}(P^\top\dot q)\bigr),\\
 F_{\mathrm{fr},i}(v_i)&=c_{c,i}\tanh\bigl(v_i/v_{\mathrm{fr}}\bigr),
\end{aligned}
 \label{eq:setup_fric}
\end{equation}
% FEEDBACK (Jasper, 2026-10-24): v_i defined (undefined variables; walk
%   W2, Dirk 2026-10-24).
where $v_i$ is the velocity of actuator $i\in\{X_1,X_2,Y\}$,
with the actuator velocities given by $P^\top\dot q$,
and $v_{\mathrm{fr}}$ sets the velocity scale of the smoothing.
For $\lvert v_i\rvert\gg v_{\mathrm{fr}}$, the friction
approaches the Coulomb law
$F_{\mathrm{fr},i}=c_{c,i}\operatorname{sign}(v_i)$
of~\cite{garcia2013model}.
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-24): c_c sentence moved here, where c_c appears;
%   v_fr tuning moved to Appendix F-C, next to its 3 v_fr check (Dirk 2026-10-24).
\mv[own]{below}{The friction levels $c_c$ are taken from Garc\'ia-Herreros et
al.~\cite[Table~I]{garcia2013model}.}
\delmv[own]{F-C}{$v_{\mathrm{fr}}=\SetupFricVzero$~mm/s was chosen by simulating
the loop with values between 0.1 and 10~mm/s.
Higher values turn the friction into viscous damping under the multisine,
and lower values keep the standstill servo error above the noise level.}
\\
% NEW (2026-10-21, Dirk): derivation of M_e; the implementation
%   (Code/Data/gantrySystemExtendedTanh.m) uses only M, C, K in A.
The added mass adds the displacement $q_a$ of $m_a$ relative to
$m_{h,r}$ along $Y$.
\add{We use the Lagrange-Euler equations of Section~\ref{sec:baseline},
adding the kinetic energy of $m_a$, the elastic energy of $k_a$
and the dissipation of $c_a$.
As in the baseline, we leave out the Coriolis and centripetal terms.}
With $q_{\mathrm e}=\begin{bmatrix}q^\top&q_a\end{bmatrix}^\top$, the
system is
\begin{equation}
 M_{\mathrm e}(Y,q_a)\,\ddot q_{\mathrm e}+C_{\mathrm e}\dot q_{\mathrm e}+K_{\mathrm e}q_{\mathrm e}
 =\begin{bmatrix}P\bigl(\uact-F_{\mathrm{fr}}(P^\top\dot q)\bigr)\\0\end{bmatrix},
 \label{eq:setup_abs}
\end{equation}
\end{subequations}
% RESTRUCTURE (own, 2026-10-24): the matrix block of M_e, M_a, C_e, K_e
%   moved verbatim to Appendix F-A (display math cannot be struck; the
%   original is the block there), heaviest part of the page, Maarten "kan
%   wel wat korter" (Dirk 2026-10-24).
\add[own]{\kwtwo{where $M_{\mathrm e}$, $C_{\mathrm e}$ and $K_{\mathrm e}$
are given in Appendix~\ref{app:setup_system}.}}
\delmv[own]{F-A}{where $M(Y)$ is \mbox{\eqref{eq:mass_matrix}} with $m_h$ the total payload mass.
$M_a(Y,\ell)$ corrects it for $m_a$ being at $Y+\ell$ instead of $Y$,
where $\ell=L_0+q_a$ and $L_0$ is the offset of the added mass along $Y$.}
% FEEDBACK (Dirk 2026-10-24): k_a, c_a to Appendix F-A with the matrices;
%   no values in the text, as for the baseline (the W3 values sentence
%   deleted); f_a is no longer used as a symbol in the main text.
\delmv[own]{F-A}{$k_a=m_a(2\pi f_a)^2$ and
$c_a=2\zeta_a\sqrt{k_am_a}$, with natural frequency $f_a$
and damping ratio $\zeta_a$.}
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-24): repeats the M_a sentence (Dirk 2026-10-24).
\del[own]{The added mass changes the inertia through $M_a$,
which also includes its coupling to $\Theta$ and $Y$.}
We simulate the system with fixed-step RK4 at
\chg[own]{$f_{\mathrm s}$}{$f_{\mathrm{sim}}$}$=20$~kHz.
% FEEDBACK (own, 2026-10-21): f_s renamed f_sim, since 1/T_s = 4 kHz
%   (sec2-rate-review; Dirk 2026-10-21).
All parameter values are listed in Table~\ref{tab:nominal_parameters}.
\delmv[own]{above}{The friction levels $c_c$ are taken from Garc\'ia-Herreros et
al.~\mbox{\cite[Table~I]{garcia2013model}}.}

%   K_1 / K_fb change

\subsection{Physical parameters and identifiable combinations}\label{sec:params}
\ifdraft
\begin{itemize}
\item With $q$ measured, known force scale and full actuation, the input-output behaviour fixes $M_0,M_1,M_2,C,K$ and conversely (this work)
\item Twelve nonzero entries, three equal to $m_h$, leave ten independent functions: exactly ten combinations are structurally identifiable (this work; definition Ovchinnikov)
\item Written physically as $\theta_{\mathrm{base}}$, the gantry counterpart of base parameters (Gautier and Khalil); one-to-one with the entries for $m_h>0$ (this work)
\item Four lost directions; estimates reported in $\theta_{\mathrm{base}}$; result independent of the encoder; augmented model in Section~IV; recovery from the records in Setup
\item Positive $\theta_{\mathrm{base}}$ does not give $M(Y)\succ0$; that holds iff \eqref{eq:lfr_admissibility} (this work; proof Appendix~\ref{app:lfr-wellposed})
\item Training keeps \eqref{eq:lfr_admissibility} at every iterate; the map and its justification are in Section~\ref{sec:aug_closed_loop}
\end{itemize}
\fi
The physical parameters are estimated jointly with the
augmentation\del[M-mail]{ (Section~\ref{sec:augmentation})}, and \chg[own]{interpretability requires
that their estimates are unique (Section~\mbox{\ref{sec:intro}})}{we
require that their identifiable combinations are estimated uniquely
(Section~\mbox{\ref{sec:problem}})}.

  \label{eq:phi}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Orthogonal-by-construction parametrisation}\label{sec:obc_construction}
\ifdraft
\begin{itemize}
\item Gy\"or\"ok's construction as adopted: baseline linear in its parameters, regressor at measured input-output data (past outputs, past and current inputs), stacked over the training data; lower case per sample, upper case stacked (2026 Eqs.~(1), (2), (5))
\item $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the least-squares fit of the network output by the regressor; its fitted part is removed and the remainder is orthogonal to $\Phi$ on the training data (2026 Eqs.~(8) to (11), Lemma~3)
\item $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ exists for full column rank of $\Phi$: identifiable baseline, weakly persistently exciting input (2026 Eqs.~(6), (7), Assumption~1)
\item Data-driven: orthogonality holds on the data used, the projection depends on their distribution; any fixed set may be used, the analysis uses the whole training set (2026 Sec.~3.2, text after Eqs.~(12), (13))
\item Uniqueness of $\hat\theta_{\mathrm b}$ shown under Assumption~1 and exact reproduction of the noise-free dynamics on the same training data (2026 Sec.~4.2, Assumption~6)
\end{itemize}
\fi
For a baseline linear in its parameters,
$\hat y_k=\varphi(x_k)\theta_{\mathrm b}$,
changing $\theta_{\mathrm b}$ changes the model output $\hat y_k$
by a linear combination of the columns of the
regressor $\varphi(x_k)$~\cite[Eqs.~(2), (39)]{gyorok2026obc}.
Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ subtract from the neural network output
its least-squares fit by the stacked
regressor~\cite[Eqs.~(8), (9), (11), Lemma~3]{gyorok2026obc}:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \hat Y&=\Phi\theta_{\mathrm b}+\tilde F^{\mathrm{ANN}},\\
 \tilde F^{\mathrm{ANN}}&=F^{\mathrm{ANN}}-\Phi\theta_{\mathrm{aux}},\\
 \theta_{\mathrm{aux}}&=\bigl(\Phi^\top\Phi\bigr)^{-1}\Phi^\top F^{\mathrm{ANN}},\\
 0&=\Phi^\top\tilde F^{\mathrm{ANN}},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_gyorok}
\end{equation}
where $x_k$ is the vector of past measured outputs and past and current
inputs~\cite[Eq.~(1)]{gyorok2026obc}, $\hat Y$ stacks the
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Dirk): "training data" -> D_N, the name since Section II.
predicted outputs over \chg[own]{the training data}{\kwtwo{$\mathcal D_N$}}, $\Phi$ is the stacked
regressor, $F^{\mathrm{ANN}}$ stacks the parallel network
outputs~\cite[Eq.~(5)]{gyorok2026obc} and $\tilde F^{\mathrm{ANN}}$ is the
projected network output~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (10)]{gyorok2026obc}.
\\
The projected network output $\tilde F^{\mathrm{ANN}}$ is
orthogonal to the regressor~\cite[Lemma~3]{gyorok2026obc}.
Calculating $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ requires
$(\Phi^\top\Phi)^{-1}$, which exists only if $\Phi$ has
full column rank~\cite[Assumption~1]{gyorok2026obc}.
Therefore different values of $\theta_{\mathrm b}$ are unable 
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Dirk): "training data" -> D_N; no "call".
to give the same stacked prediction on \chg[own]{the training data}{\kwtwo{$\mathcal D_N$}}.
\chg[Dirk]{Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ call an input with this property}{\kwtwo{An input with this property is}} persistently
exciting~\cite[Eq.~(6), Sec.~4.3]{gyorok2026obc}.
This also requires an identifiable baseline, where different
values of $\theta_{\mathrm b}$ give different functions
$\varphi(\cdot)\theta_{\mathrm b}$.
\subsection{Extension to the gantry}\label{sec:obc_map}
\ifdraft
\begin{itemize}
\item Three differences, each changing one element of \eqref{eq:obc_gyorok}: regressor, data, prediction (this work)
\item Regressor: Jacobian of the normalised transition in $\beta$ at $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$, since the baseline is nonlinear through $M(Y)^{-1}$; $\beta$ because only the ten combinations are identifiable (adapted from Gy\"or\"ok 2025 Sec.~4, Eq.~(15); 2026 Assumption~1; Section~II-C; D-190, D-229); offset column $\Gamma$ included (D-257)
\item Data: reference tuples reconstructed from the measured positions, regressor at the data as in 2026 Eq.~(5) rather than at a simulated baseline (2025 Sec.~3); each with a successor; built once before training (D-252, D-254)
\item Projection on the stacked tuples, with the orthogonality of the section opening as its last line; holds for the stack at $\bar x=0$ (adapted from 2026 Eqs.~(8) to (11), Lemma~3)
\item Prediction: the correction at every step of the closed-loop state update, physical rows only; coefficient differentiated (2026 Eqs.~(9), (10), (13); added states this work)
\end{itemize}
\fi
Our baseline violates three requirements of the projection in
\eqref{eq:obc_gyorok}.
\chg{Its}{\kwtwo{First, its}} state update is nonlinear in the parameters, because
the next state update depends on $M(Y)^{-1}$ in \eqref{eq:base_ss},
violating the linear requirement for the regressor.
Instead of the regressor the Jacobian of the baseline state update is taken 
with respect to $\beta$,
as in the orthogonal regularisation method of
Gy\"or\"ok et al.~\cite[Sec.~4, Eq.~(15)]{gyorok2025l4dc}.
Like the regressor, the stacked Jacobian must have full column rank.

\subsection{Extension to the gantry}\label{sec:obc_map}
\ifdraft
\begin{itemize}
\item Three differences, each changing one element of \eqref{eq:obc_gyorok}: regressor, data, prediction (this work)
\item Regressor: Jacobian of the normalised transition in $\beta$ at $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$, since the baseline is nonlinear through $M(Y)^{-1}$; $\beta$ because only the ten combinations are identifiable (adapted from Gy\"or\"ok 2025 Sec.~4, Eq.~(15); 2026 Assumption~1; Section~II-C; D-190, D-229); offset column $\Gamma$ included (D-257)

\end{itemize}

Our baseline violates three requirements of the projection in
\eqref{eq:obc_gyorok}.
\chg{Its}{\kwtwo{First, its}} state update is nonlinear in the parameters, because
the next state update depends on $M(Y)^{-1}$ in \eqref{eq:base_ss},
violating the linear requirement for the regressor.
Instead of the regressor the Jacobian of the baseline state update is taken 
with respect to $\beta$,
as in the orthogonal regularisation method of
Gy\"or\"ok et al.~\cite[Sec.~4, Eq.~(15)]{gyorok2025l4dc}.
Like the regressor, the stacked Jacobian must have full column rank.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Jasper v1 p8 JsV1 "what is beta"; Dirk): back-reference.
This requires identifiable parameters, which is why we use $\beta$\add[JsV1]{\kwtwo{ (Section~\mbox{\ref{sec:params}})}}.
The Jacobian is taken at a linearisation point $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$ as
\begin{equation}
 \varphi(\beta_{\mathrm{lin}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n})
 =\left.\frac{\partial f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}\bigl(\theta_{\mathrm{base}}(\beta),\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n}\bigr)}
   {\partial\beta}\right|_{\beta=\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}},
\label{eq:obc_sens}
\end{equation}
where $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}\in\R^{10}$ and
$\varphi:\R^{10}\times\R^6\times\R^3\to\R^{6\times10}$.
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Dirk): offset block reworded with Gyorok 2025 PDF p7
%   wording around Eq. (16); "so"/"because" tails and "part of" cut; the
%   Eq. (18) reason says what the column does.
\chg[Dirk]{\kw{The linearisation also leaves an offset that does not depend on
$\beta$}}{\kwtwo{Expanding \eqref{eq:obc_sens} gives}}\kw{~\cite[Eq.~(16)]{gyorok2025l4dc}:}
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}\bigl(\theta_{\mathrm{base}}(\beta),\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n}\bigr)
 &\approx\varphi\,\beta+\gamma,\\
 \gamma
 &=f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}\bigl(\theta_{\mathrm{base}}(\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}),\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n}\bigr)
  -\varphi\,\beta_{\mathrm{lin}},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_offset}
\end{equation}
\kw{where} \add[Dirk]{\kwtwo{the first term is linear in $\beta$ and}} \kw{$\gamma:\R^{10}\times\R^6\times\R^3\to\R^6$}\chg[Dirk]{\kw{, so that
$\varphi\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}+\gamma$ is the next state predicted by the
baseline at $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$}}{\kwtwo{ is an offset independent of $\beta$}}.
\kw{Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ add this offset as an extra column to the Jacobian, to}
\chg[Dirk]{\kw{include all components of the baseline model in the
orthogonality}}{\kwtwo{make the neural network also orthogonal to the next
states predicted by the baseline}}\kw{~\cite[Eq.~(18)]{gyorok2025l4dc}.
We include it as well}\del[Dirk]{\kw{, so the neural network has no component along the
stacked next states predicted by the baseline}}.
% RESTRUCTURE (2026-10-19, Maarten mail): moved below eq:obc_recovery, which
%   it used before its d
sections/04_obc.tex:350 | deleted text | cite Sec.~4
\chg{The}{\kwtwo{Second, the}} Jacobian also depends on the state, while the regressor of
Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ uses only measured inputs and
outputs~\cite[Eqs.~(1), (2)]{gyorok2026obc}.
Since only the positions are measured, we evaluate the Jacobian at these
positions with the velocities reconstructed from them:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \tilde x_i&=\col(q_i,\dot q_i),\qquad q_i=P^{-\top}y_i,\\
 \dot q_i&=\frac{-q_{i+2}+8q_{i+1}-8q_{i-1}+q_{i-2}}{12\,T_s},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_tuples}
\end{equation}
where $y_i$ is the measured actuator position at sample $i$.
Each tuple $(\tilde x_i,\bar x_i,u_i)$ uses the recorded actuator 
force $u_i$ and $\bar x_i=0$,
with the physical state and input normalised to
$\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_i$ and $u^{\mathrm n}_i$
using \eqref{eq:aug_norm}.
The tuples are calculated once before training, using all samples for which
\eqref{eq:obc_tuples} can be calculated at $i$ and at the next sample $i+1$.
\\
Stacking the Jacobian, \kw{the offset} and the network output over the tuples, the projection
of \eqref{eq:obc_gyorok} becomes
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \Phi_\Gamma
 &=\col\bigl([\varphi\ \ \gamma](\beta_{\mathrm{lin}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_i,u^{\mathrm n}_i)\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I},\\
 F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})
 &=\col\bigl(f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}},\col(\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_i,0),u^{\mathrm n}_i)\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I},\\
 \theta_{\mathrm{aux}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})
 &=\bigl(\Phi_\Gamma^\top\Phi_\Gamma\bigr)^{-1}\Phi_\Gamma^\top F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),\\
 \tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})
 &=F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})-\Phi_\Gamma\,\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),\\
 0&=\Phi_\Gamma^{\top}\tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_coef}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal I$ is the set of tuples, $N=|\mathcal I|$,
\kw{$\Phi_\Gamma=[\Phi\ \Gamma]\in\R^{6N\times11}$ stacks $\varphi$ and $\gamma$}
evaluated at $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$,
$F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}},\tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}\in\R^{6N}$
and $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}\in\R^{\kw{11}}$.
The projected network output $\tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$ therefore
has no component along any column of $\kw{\Phi_\Gamma}$, which satisfies our orthogonality
definition at the start of this section.
This holds for the stacked tuples at $\bar x=0$, not for each tuple separately.
\\
\chg{We}{\kwtwo{Third, we}} use a state-space model predicting the next state instead of the output.
The fitted part is removed from the neural network correction of the
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Jasper v1 p8 JsV10 "which correction?"; Dirk): the
%   Gyorok sentence is cut, "correction" now only means f_aug; the output
%   contrast is in the "Third, ..." sentence; citation moved up.
physical state at every step in the closed-loop simulation\add[JsV10]{\kwtwo{~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (13)]{gyorok2026obc}}}.
At each step, we subtract the Jacobian \kw{and offset} multiplied by
$\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ from the network correction,
evaluated at the current state and input.
\del[JsV10]{Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ apply the same correction to the predicted
output~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (13)]{gyorok2026obc}.}
The baseline has no added states, so its Jacobian \kw{and offset are} zero
in the added-state rows and $g^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$
is orthogonal to it by definition.
We therefore only correct the physical rows:
% Only the physical rows are corrected, because the baseline has no added-state
% update:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{obc}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n})
 &=[\varphi\ \ \gamma](\beta_{\mathrm{lin}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n})\,
  \theta_{\mathrm{aux}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),\\
 \tilde x^{\mathrm n}_{k+1|\tau}
 &=f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}+f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}-f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{obc}},\\
 \bar x_{k+1|\tau}&=g^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_corr}
\end{equation}
where
$f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{obc}}:\R^{n_{\mathrm{aug}}}\times\R^6\times\R^3\to\R^6$
is evaluated at $(\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_{k|\tau},\hat u^{\mathrm n}_{k|\tau})$, and
$f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}$, $f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$ and
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Dirk): "take the arguments of" -> "are evaluated as
%   in" (the verb of the same sentence); "so ... is trained" -> "to train".
$g^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$ \chg[Dirk]{take the arguments of}{\kwtwo{are evaluated as in}} \eqref{eq:aug_loss}.
We differentiate $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ with respect to $\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}$, as
in~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (10)]{gyorok2026obc},
\chg[Dirk]{\kw{so} the network is trained}{\kwtwo{to train the network}} using the gradient of its projected output.
\subsection{Identification and recovery}\label{sec:obc_ident}
\ifdraft
\begin{itemize}

with the added-state
initialisation of Section~\ref{sec:aug_ps2}.

the projected state update \eqref{eq:obc_corr}.
Since $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ depends on $\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}$,
we solve \eqref{eq:obc_coef} at every evaluation of $V$.
At the start of each epoch $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$ is set to the current $\beta$, 
and\del[Dirk]{ it} is held fixed during the epoch.

sections/04_obc.tex:352 | deleted text | cite Sec.~4
\chg{The}{\kwtwo{Second, the}} Jacobian also depends on the state, while the regressor of
Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ uses only measured inputs and
outputs~\cite[Eqs.~(1), (2)]{gyorok2026obc}.
Since only the positions are measured, we evaluate the Jacobian at these
positions with the velocities reconstructed from them:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \tilde x_i&=\col(q_i,\dot q_i),\qquad q_i=P^{-\top}y_i,\\
 \dot q_i&=\frac{-q_{i+2}+8q_{i+1}-8q_{i-1}+q_{i-2}}{12\,T_s},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_tuples}
\end{equation}
where $y_i$ is the measured actuator position at sample $i$.
Each tuple $(\tilde x_i,\bar x_i,u_i)$ uses the recorded actuator 
force $u_i$ and $\bar x_i=0$,
with the physical state and input normalised to
$\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_i$ and $u^{\mathrm n}_i$
using \eqref{eq:aug_norm}.
The tuples are calculated once before training, using all samples for which
\eqref{eq:obc_tuples} can be calculated at $i$ and at the next sample $i+1$.
\\
Stacking the Jacobian, \kw{the offset} and the network output over the tuples, the projection
of \eqref{eq:obc_gyorok} becomes
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \Phi_\Gamma
 &=\col\bigl([\varphi\ \ \gamma](\beta_{\mathrm{lin}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_i,u^{\mathrm n}_i)\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I},\\
 F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})
 &=\col\bigl(f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}},\col(\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_i,0),u^{\mathrm n}_i)\bigr)_{i\in\mathcal I},\\
 \theta_{\mathrm{aux}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})
 &=\bigl(\Phi_\Gamma^\top\Phi_\Gamma\bigr)^{-1}\Phi_\Gamma^\top F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),\\
 \tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})
 &=F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}})-\Phi_\Gamma\,\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),\\
 0&=\Phi_\Gamma^{\top}\tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_coef}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal I$ is the set of tuples, $N=|\mathcal I|$,
\kw{$\Phi_\Gamma=[\Phi\ \Gamma]\in\R^{6N\times11}$ stacks $\varphi$ and $\gamma$}
evaluated at $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$,
$F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}},\tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}\in\R^{6N}$
and $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}\in\R^{\kw{11}}$.
The projected network output $\tilde F^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$ therefore
has no component along any column of $\kw{\Phi_\Gamma}$, which satisfies our orthogonality
definition at the start of this section.
This holds for the stacked tuples at $\bar x=0$, not for each tuple separately.
\\
\chg{We}{\kwtwo{Third, we}} use a state-space model predicting the next state instead of the output.
The fitted part is removed from the neural network correction of the
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Jasper v1 p8 JsV10 "which correction?"; Dirk): the
%   Gyorok sentence is cut, "correction" now only means f_aug; the output
%   contrast is in the "Third, ..." sentence; citation moved up.
physical state at every step in the closed-loop simulation\add[JsV10]{\kwtwo{~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (13)]{gyorok2026obc}}}.
At each step, we subtract the Jacobian \kw{and offset} multiplied by
$\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ from the network correction,
evaluated at the current state and input.
\del[JsV10]{Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ apply the same correction to the predicted
output~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (13)]{gyorok2026obc}.}
The baseline has no added states, so its Jacobian \kw{and offset are} zero
in the added-state rows and $g^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$
is orthogonal to it by definition.
We therefore only correct the physical rows:
% Only the physical rows are corrected, because the baseline has no added-state
% update:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{obc}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n})
 &=[\varphi\ \ \gamma](\beta_{\mathrm{lin}},\tilde x^{\mathrm n},u^{\mathrm n})\,
  \theta_{\mathrm{aux}}(\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}),\\
 \tilde x^{\mathrm n}_{k+1|\tau}
 &=f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}+f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}-f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{obc}},\\
 \bar x_{k+1|\tau}&=g^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}},
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:obc_corr}
\end{equation}
where
$f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{obc}}:\R^{n_{\mathrm{aug}}}\times\R^6\times\R^3\to\R^6$
is evaluated at $(\tilde x^{\mathrm n}_{k|\tau},\hat u^{\mathrm n}_{k|\tau})$, and
$f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{base}}$, $f^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$ and
% FEEDBACK (2026-10-23, Dirk): "take the arguments of" -> "are evaluated as
%   in" (the verb of the same sentence); "so ... is trained" -> "to train".
$g^{\mathrm n}_{\mathrm{aug}}$ \chg[Dirk]{take the arguments of}{\kwtwo{are evaluated as in}} \eqref{eq:aug_loss}.
We differentiate $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ with respect to $\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}$, as
in~\cite[Eqs.~(9), (10)]{gyorok2026obc},
\chg[Dirk]{\kw{so} the network is trained}{\kwtwo{to train the network}} using the gradient of its projected output.

With orthogonality by construction the state update in \eqref{eq:aug_loss} is instead
the projected state update \eqref{eq:obc_corr}.
Since $\theta_{\mathrm{aux}}$ depends on $\theta_{\mathrm{aug}}$,
we solve \eqref{eq:obc_coef} at every evaluation of $V$.
At the start of each epoch $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$ is set to the current $\beta$, 
and\del[Dirk]{ it} is held fixed during the epoch.

which requires rebuilding $\Phi_\Gamma$ at each evaluation

keep $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$ fixed at the nominal parameters,
assuming these are close to the true parameters~\cite[Sec.~4]{gyorok2025l4dc}.}{\kwtwo{Gy\"or\"ok et al.\ update $\beta_{\mathrm{lin}}$ at every iteration
or keep it fixed at the nominal parameters~\cite[Sec.~4]{gyorok2025l4dc}.}}

we instead adapt their recomputation 
at the start of each epoch~\cite[Remark~2]{gyorok2025l4dc}.

\del[M-mail]{We load the best checkpoint and rebuild $\Phi_\Gamma$ using its $\beta$.

\item Grey-box dynamic augmentation is the target compromise: preserve the baseline and learn only the missing state dynamics \cite{hoekstra2026lfr}
\end{itemize}

White-box models are attractive because they reflect the physics of the
system, which makes them interpretable.
First-principles (FP) models are a specific type of white-box model,
derived from physical laws and described by quantities such as mass,
stiffness, and damping.
However, purely physics-based models do not always capture all behaviour
needed for accurate prediction across the operating range
\cite{willard2020integrating}.
More accurate FP models can be developed, but this is labour-intensive
\cite{hoekstra2026lfr}.

\iffalse
\begin{itemize}
\item Settling prediction limits throughput in coupled high-precision gantries, so model error has a direct operational cost \cite{garcia2013model}
\item The concrete digital-twin use case is to evaluate relevant ASMPT motion and a changed controller before deployment on the machine
\item The physics model exposes masses, stiffnesses, damping, and coupling, but omits position-dependent flexible dynamics that matter for prediction
\item A black-box model offers flexibility but weakens extrapolation arguments and removes parameters useful for control design, digital twins, and health monitoring
\item Grey-box dynamic augmentation is the target compromise: preserve the baseline and learn only the missing state dynamics \cite{hoekstra2026lfr}
\end{itemize}
\fi
